findings.title: A restore of an older backup brings back revoked or erased staff access, and the ledger's privacy_erase_staff line then fails instead of reapplying
findings.evidence:
privacy-data-map.md:48: "After any restore, and before the site reopens, run every line again: both functions are safe to repeat."
privacy_requests.sql:33-35:
  if exists (select 1 from public.staff s where s.user_id = p_user and s.active) then
    raise exception 'Revoke the member in the team screen first.'
staff-admin/index.ts:114-120: the revoke is only staff.active=false plus an Auth ban_duration, both rows in the database.
findings.failureScenario: Day 1: Anas runs pnpm backup. Day 5: he revokes a departed editor (active=false, Auth ban) and erases them (privacy_erase_staff, ledger line written). Day 10: the project is lost and he restores the day-1 file. The restored staff row is active=true, auth.users has no ban and still has the real email, identities, sessions and refresh tokens. He follows the runbook and re-runs the ledger line: it raises 'Revoke the member in the team screen first.' (object_not_in_prerequisite_state), so the erasure is not reapplied. Nothing tells him to re-revoke. The runbook's revoke step is never written to the ledger, so a member who was revoked but not erased is also active again, and can sign in by email code with their old role. The restore steps in docs/operations.md (511-532) do not mention the ledger at all, so following operations.md alone reopens the site with erased contacts and staff data back.
findings.suggestedFix: Docs only. In docs/privacy-data-map.md, write every revoke to the deletion ledger as well as every erase. Change line 48 to say: after a restore, first revoke every member the ledger lists in the team screen, then re-run the erase lines. Add a step 7 to 'A real restore into a new hosted project' in docs/operations.md: reapply the deletion ledger (revokes first) before the site reopens. The app is unchanged. The erase function keeps its guard against erasing an active member.
verifierCorrections: Docs only, as suggested. Also in privacy-data-map.md 'A departed staff member', add revoke as a ledger step, e.g. `update public.staff set active=false where user_id='<id>'` plus the ban (re-run through the team screen after a restore). In operations.md, the new step 7 must come before the site reopens: re-revoke every member the ledger lists, then re-run the erase lines.

findings.title: Guide's db:import and db:demo-catalog steps fail: DATABASE_URL is never set by db:env and the scripts read only process.env
findings.evidence:
docs/development.md:127-129
```sh
pnpm db:reset
pnpm db:import           # imports content/initial-content.json, skips already-published docs
```
scripts/import-content.mjs:20-23
```js
const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL
if (!dbUrl) {
  console.error('Refusing: DATABASE_URL is not set.')
```
scripts/local-env.mjs writes only NEXT_PUBLIC_* and the function values. It writes no DATABASE_URL, and a plain `node` script loads no .env file. CI passes it by hand (ci.yml:80-81 `env: DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres`).
findings.failureScenario: A new developer follows the P04 block or line 79 in a fresh shell. `pnpm db:import` exits 1 with 'Refusing: DATABASE_URL is not set.', and `pnpm db:demo-catalog` does the same. Line 27 also claims `pnpm db:env` "writes everything local development needs", so nothing in the guide tells them where the value comes from. The later `pnpm build` then fails or exports empty pages because nothing is published.
findings.suggestedFix: In docs/development.md, change line 128 to `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres pnpm db:import`. Show the same prefix for `pnpm db:demo-catalog` at line 79. Replace line 27's "writes everything local development needs from the running local stack" with "writes the values Next, the Edge Functions and the tests read from the running local stack; `DATABASE_URL` (and `TEST_ENV` for `pnpm test:db`) are passed on the command line, as in the commands below".
